cases.sentence: Толстый, выше ___, широкий, с огромными красными руками, он, как говорится, не умел войти в салон и еще менее умел из него выйти, то есть перед выходом сказать что-нибудь особенно приятное.
cases.explain: «обыкновенного роста» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Pierre was ungainly. Stout, about the average height, broad, with huge red hands; he did not know, as the saying is, how to enter a drawing room and still less how to leave one; that is, how to say something particularly agreeable before going away. Besides this he was absentminded. When he rose to go, he took up instead of his own, the general’s three-cornered hat, and held it, pulling at the plume, till the general asked him to restore it. All his absentmindedness and inability to enter a room and converse in it was, however, redeemed by his kindly, simple, and modest expression. Anna Pávlovna turned toward him and, with a Christian mildness that expressed forgiveness of his indiscretion, nodded and said: “I hope to see you again, but I also hope you will change your opinions, my dear Monsieur Pierre.”

cases.sentence: Вставая, он вместо своей шляпы захватил трехугольную шляпу с ___ и держал ее, дергая султан, до тех пор, пока генерал не попросил возвратить ее.
cases.explain: «генеральским плюмажем» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Pierre was ungainly. Stout, about the average height, broad, with huge red hands; he did not know, as the saying is, how to enter a drawing room and still less how to leave one; that is, how to say something particularly agreeable before going away. Besides this he was absentminded. When he rose to go, he took up instead of his own, the general’s three-cornered hat, and held it, pulling at the plume, till the general asked him to restore it. All his absentmindedness and inability to enter a room and converse in it was, however, redeemed by his kindly, simple, and modest expression. Anna Pávlovna turned toward him and, with a Christian mildness that expressed forgiveness of his indiscretion, nodded and said: “I hope to see you again, but I also hope you will change your opinions, my dear Monsieur Pierre.”

cases.sentence: Князь Ипполит стоял возле хорошенькой ___ и упорно смотрел прямо на нее в лорнет.
cases.explain: «беременной княгини» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy had gone out into the hall, and, turning his shoulders to the footman who was helping him on with his cloak, listened indifferently to his wife’s chatter with Prince Ippolit who had also come into the hall. Prince Ippolit stood close to the pretty, pregnant princess, and stared fixedly at her through his eyeglass.

cases.sentence: — Идите, Annette, вы простудитесь, — говорила ___, прощаясь с Анной Павловной.
cases.explain: «маленькая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Go in, Annette, or you will catch cold,” said the little princess, taking leave of Anna Pávlovna. “It is settled,” she added in a low voice.

cases.sentence: Анна Павловна уже успела переговорить с Лизой о сватовстве, которое она затевала между Анатолем и золовкой ___.
cases.explain: «маленькой княгини» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Anna Pávlovna had already managed to speak to Liza about the match she contemplated between Anatole and the little princess’ sister-in-law.

cases.sentence: — Я надеюсь на вас, ___, — сказала Анна Павловна тоже тихо, — вы напишете к ней и скажете мне, comment le père envisagera la chose. Au revoir,[97] как отец посмотрит на дело.
cases.explain: «милый друг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I rely on you, my dear,” said Anna Pávlovna, also in a low tone. “Write to her and let me know how her father looks at the matter. Au revoir!”—and she left the hall.

cases.sentence: Князь Ипполит подошел к ___ и, близко наклоняя к ней свое лицо, стал полушопотом что-то говорить ей.
cases.explain: «маленькой княгине» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Prince Ippolit approached the little princess and, bending his face close to her, began to whisper something.

cases.explain: «Прекрасный вечер» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I am very glad I did not go to the ambassador’s,” said Prince Ippolit “—so dull—. It has been a delightful evening, has it not? Delightful!”

cases.explain: «красивые женщины» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “They say the ball will be very good,” replied the princess, drawing up her downy little lip. “All the pretty women in society will be there.”

cases.sentence: — Je plains le pauvre mari, ce petit officier, qui se donne des airs de prince régnant.[100] А знаете ли, вы ужасны с вашим ___.
cases.explain: «невинным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Do you know, you are a terrible chap for all your innocent airs,” continued the vicomte. “I pity the poor husband, that little officer who gives himself the airs of a monarch.”

cases.sentence: Я жалею ___, этого офицерика, который корчит из себя владетельную особу
cases.explain: «бедного мужа» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Do you know, you are a terrible chap for all your innocent airs,” continued the vicomte. “I pity the poor husband, that little officer who gives himself the airs of a monarch.”
